text:
Devon: Quick sync — we need to finalize guardrails for autoscale fallbacks, tenant spillover, and quota ownership before we lock the Q3 Dedicated roadmap. Prefer a short, actionable decision today.
Ana: model-variant fallback first. keeps latency predictable and avoids cross-tenant mixing. :+1:
Mike: model-variant is good as default but some enterprise customers require strict regional isolation — we should allow tenant-level opt-out for region fallbacks.
Priya: +1 for opt-out. Proposed default order: model-variant -> same-region shard spillover -> elastic buffer (soft) -> hosted fallback (hard).
Sara: ops concern: spillover can blow up cost if many tenants spike. need per-tenant burst credits + a hard cap that enforces throttling when exceeded.
Devon: agreed. proposal: two-tier quota model = committed reserved quota + transient burst credits (daily replenish). when burst exhausted, apply priority rules and then throttle.
Ana: can we represent that as config? example: 
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  fallback_order: [model_variant, region_spill, elastic_buffer, hosted_fallback]
  quotas:
    reserved_units: 1000
    burst_credits: 500
    burst_replenish_interval: 24h
  hard_cap_behavior: throttle
  tenant_opt_out: true
```
Mike: also need visibility: token cost delta, p95 latency, and spillover eviction counts surfaced in Console. customers will ask for ROI numbers.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary plan created — will route 3 pilot tenants to new autoscale policy in staging on Tue.
Priya: launch criteria we should track: docs + migration guide, tenant opt-in flow, canary w/ 3 customers, and a rollback plan.
Sara: rollback criteria suggestion: abort if canary shows >2x cost delta or >2x p95 latency vs baseline or any data-isolation violations.
Devon: action items: @Ana write RFC by Friday (include sample config, migration steps, opt-out UX), @Mike add metrics & a spillover heatmap to dashboards, @Sara define hard-cap enforcement & alerts. I will coordinate canary accounts.
Ana: will draft RFC — will include CLI examples and a short migration checklist.
Mike: will add Grafana panels and a cost-compare dashboard tile.
Sara: I'll own cap enforcement code + tests and add alert thresholds.
Devon: thanks — plan to ship to staging next week, then 2-week canary. :rocket:
